Add an imperial-unit scale bar to a ggplot map

Source: R/map_scale_bar.R
mysterymaps_scale_bar.Rd

Thin wrapper around ggspatial::annotation_scale() that defaults to miles instead of kilometers.

Usage

mysterymaps_scale_bar(
  location = "bl",
  width_hint = 0.25,
  unit_category = "imperial",
  ...
)

Arguments

location

character(1): corner to place the bar in – one of "bl", "br", "tl", "tr".

width_hint

numeric(1): target width as a fraction of the plot panel.

unit_category

character(1): passed through to ggspatial::annotation_scale(). Default "imperial"; pass "metric" or "SI" to override.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to ggspatial::annotation_scale() (e.g. bar_cols, text_cex, pad_x).

Value

A ggplot2 layer, addable to a plot with +.

Details

unit_category = "imperial" is accepted by annotation_scale() only through its ... forwarding – it does not appear in the function's own formal arguments (args(ggspatial::annotation_scale) omits it). A caller who does not already know that can reasonably assume the function has no imperial option and ship a kilometer bar on a United States map, silently: there is no error or warning either way. This wrapper exists so every static map in this package picks up miles by default without each caller having to rediscover the ...-forwarding behaviour.

See also

Other mapping: mysterymaps_bivariate_choropleth_map(), mysterymaps_cartogram_map(), mysterymaps_catchment_redundancy_map(), mysterymaps_clear_isochrone_cache(), mysterymaps_create_isochrones(), mysterymaps_flow_map(), mysterymaps_hrr_maps(), mysterymaps_isochrones_for_df(), mysterymaps_jitter_points(), mysterymaps_map_acceptance_rate(), mysterymaps_map_acog_districts(), mysterymaps_map_base(), mysterymaps_map_block_group(), mysterymaps_map_leaflet(), mysterymaps_map_physicians(), mysterymaps_pathway_small_multiples_map(), mysterymaps_plot_isochrones(), mysterymaps_rate_choropleth_map()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("ggspatial", quietly = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + mysterymaps_scale_bar()
}
